{{technical|date=April 2016}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''fundamental theorem of topos theory''' states that the [[comma category|slice]] <math>\mathbf{E} / X</math> of an [[elementary topos]] <math>\mathbf{E}</math> over any one of its [[object (category theory)|objects]] <math>X</math> is itself a topos. Moreover, if there is a [[morphism]] <math>f : A \rightarrow B </math> in <math>\mathbf{E}</math> then there is a [[functor]] <math>f^*: \mathbf{E} / B \rightarrow \mathbf{E} / A </math> which preserves [[exponential object|exponentials]] and the [[subobject classifier]].

== The pullback functor ==
For any morphism ''f'' in <math>\mathbf{E}</math> there is an associated "pullback functor" <math> f^* := - \mapsto f \times - \rightarrow f </math> which is key in the proof of the theorem. For any other morphism ''g'' in <math>\mathbf{E}</math> which shares the same [[codomain]] as ''f'', their product <math>f \times g</math> is the diagonal of their pullback square, and the morphism which goes from the domain of <math>f \times g</math> to the domain of ''f'' is opposite to ''g'' in the pullback square, so it is the pullback of ''g'' along ''f'', which can be denoted as <math>f^*g</math>.

Note that a topos <math>\mathbf{E}</math> is isomorphic to the slice over its own [[Initial and terminal objects|terminal object]], i.e. <math>\mathbf{E} \cong \mathbf{E} / 1</math>, so for any object ''A'' in <math>\mathbf{E}</math> there is a morphism <math>f : A \rightarrow 1 </math> and thereby a pullback functor <math>f^* : \mathbf{E} \rightarrow \mathbf{E} / A</math>, which is why any slice <math>\mathbf{E} / A </math> is also a topos.

For a given slice <math>\mathbf{E} / B</math> let <math>X \over B</math> denote an object of it, where ''X'' is an object of the base category. Then <math>B^*</math> is a functor which maps: <math> - \mapsto {B \times - \over B} </math>. Now apply <math>f^*</math> to <math>B^*</math>. This yields
: <math>f^* B^* : - \mapsto {B \times - \over B} \mapsto {{A \over B} \times {B \times - \over B} \over {A \over B}} \cong {\Big({A \times_B \, B \times - \over B}\Big) \over {A \over B}} \cong {A \times_B B \times - \over A} \cong {A \times - \over A} = A^*</math>
so this is how the pullback functor <math>f^*</math> maps objects of <math>\mathbf{E} / B</math> to <math>\mathbf{E} / A</math>. Furthermore, note that any element ''C'' of the base topos is isomorphic to <math>{1 \times C \over 1} = 1^* C</math>, therefore if <math>f : A \rightarrow 1</math> then <math>f^*: 1^* \rightarrow A^*</math> and <math>f^* : C \mapsto A^* C </math> so that <math>f^*</math> is indeed a functor from the base topos <math>\mathbf{E}</math> to its slice <math>\mathbf{E} / A</math>.

== Logical interpretation ==
Consider a pair of ground formulas <math>\phi</math> and <math>\psi</math> whose extensions <math>[\_|\phi]</math> and <math>[\_|\psi]</math> (where the underscore here denotes the null context) are objects of the base topos. Then <math>\phi</math> implies <math>\psi</math> if and only if there is a monic from <math>[\_|\phi]</math> to <math>[\_|\psi]</math>. If these are the case then, by theorem, the formula <math>\psi</math> is true in the slice <math>\mathbf{E} / [\_|\phi]</math>, because the terminal object <math>[\_|\phi] \over [\_|\phi]</math> of the slice factors through its extension <math>[\_|\psi]</math>. In logical terms, this could be expressed as
:<math>\vdash \phi \rightarrow \psi \over \phi \vdash \psi</math>
so that slicing <math>\mathbf{E}</math> by the extension of <math>\phi</math> would correspond to assuming <math>\phi</math> as a hypothesis. Then the theorem would say that making a logical assumption does not change the rules of topos logic.
